- File: .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py
  Line or code reference: parse_immediate_block() — the `markers = list(SESSION_MARKER_RE.finditer(text))` plus `if not markers or markers[-1].group(1) != session_label: return None` block
  Problem: The new code takes the LAST marker in the body and returns None when that marker is for a session other than the queried one. The old code filtered markers to the queried session first, then took the last one. In a comment body that contains an immediate block for the queried session followed by an immediate block for a different session (the cross-session case the new design does not test), the old code returned the queried session's block; the new code returns None. `lookup()` in this repo iterates through issue/PR comments and parses each, so a single comment shared between sessions (e.g. two unattended stages reporting the same pattern) can now fail to surface the earlier session's report.
  Why it fails at runtime: a comment body of `<SESSION_A_BLOCK>\n\n<SESSION_B_BLOCK>` causes `parse_immediate_block(body, SESSION_A)` to return None instead of SESSION_A's block. The downstream poller that reads `lookup` output would silently miss the earlier session's prompt, delaying the operator's notification.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py
  Line or code reference: parse_immediate_block() — the `fields.rfind(f"\n{IMMEDIATE_HEADING}\n") ... elif fields.startswith(f"{IMMEDIATE_HEADING}\n"): ... else: return None` chain
  Problem: When the heading sits at the end of `fields` without a trailing newline (i.e. fields ends with `<heading>` rather than `<heading>\n`), neither `rfind` (no `\n` after the heading) nor `startswith` (heading is not at position 0) matches, so the parser returns None. immediate_block's normal layout always emits `\n\n` after the heading, so this requires a malformed or hand-edited body — but a body where someone trimmed the trailing newline of the heading line would silently produce a None instead of a parsed dict.
  Why it fails at runtime: A hand-edited or partially redacted body that omits the `\n` after `**Immediate report**` will fail to parse even when the fence and marker are intact, returning None where the old code (which searched for the heading on the same string without requiring the trailing `\n` for the `startswith` fallback) would have parsed correctly.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
